text:
alexa: quick thread  about bulk label-edit in scorecards + the confirm CTA microcopy. put mocks in figma: https://www.figma.com/file/label-edit/proto
chris: skimmed. main UX tradeoff: inline batch edit (fast, contextual) vs modal confirm (safer, more room for details). which do we prefer for the default flow?
min: leaning modal for destructive label ops (remove/replace). For additive labels maybe inline tag-picker is fine. People often expect an undo for bulk changes.
fer: copy copy: current confirm reads "Apply labels to selected results?" feels passive. analytics team wants clear verbs: `labels.apply.confirm`. propose "Apply labels to X results" with secondary hint "This will update results in place. Undo available for 5s.".
alexa: good. also keyboard accessibility: if modal opens, focus on primary CTA and trap focus. screen readers should announce count and label names. example announce: "Confirm label apply, 12 results selected. Primary action: Apply labels."
chris: compact-mode concern: modals are jarring on small screens. propose using a bottom-sheet on <420px that still has same semantics and focus handling.
min: a11y nit: don't only rely on color to show that a label was added. add a checkmark icon and an `aria-live` update like "2 labels applied to result 7". For batch, a single `aria-live` summary is better: "Labels applied to 12 results."
fer: undo UX: optimistic update + toast with "Undo" is fast. but if user navigates away, server side revert should still be possible. store undo token in response and call revert endpoint when Undo clicked. analytics event `labels.apply.undo`.
a11y-bot: accessibility-scan: recommend confirm dialog include `role=dialog`, `aria-labelledby` pointing to heading, and a visible focus indicator. Also ensure the live region message is placed before focus shifts.
alexa: microcopy variants for primary CTA: A) "Apply labels" B) "Apply to 12 results" C) "Add labels". Which is clearest?
chris: prefer B for explicit scope. reduces accidental clicks. keep CTA width responsive though.
min: for screen readers, longer label is fine. Visually we can show shorter `Apply` and set `aria-label="Apply labels to 12 results"` on button.
fer: accessibility for tag-picker: when replacing labels, show a clear radio toggle: "Add" vs "Replace" with `aria-pressed` states and help text. default to Add to avoid data loss.
alexa: analytics: fire `labels.apply.started` when user opens the confirm step, `labels.apply.confirm` on success, include properties `count`, `operation` (add/replace/remove), `label_ids`.
chris: keyboard shortcut idea: while multi-select is active, `l` opens label-edit; `Shift+L` opens full modal. document in shortcuts page.
min: implementation note: avoid re-rendering every row on optimistic update; instead update row state locally and reconcile with server response. highlight changed cells briefly (3s) with motion respecting `prefers-reduced-motion`.
a11y-bot: suggested aria live text examples: on success: "12 results updated: labels X, Y applied. Undo available." on failure: "Could not apply labels to 4 results. See details.". Keep these under 250 chars.
fer: mobile touch targets: label chips should be tappable and min 44x44. tag-picker modal should be full-bleed and support pinch-to-zoom for accessibility.
alexa: copy for toast: "12 results updated. Undo" and button `Undo`. toast should have `role=status` or `role=alert` depending on urgency; prefer polite for non-blocking.
chris: testing: unit tests for focus trap + restore, e2e for optimistic apply -> undo -> reconcile failure path. add an accessibility e2e that validates live region announcements.
min: i'll update figma with the modal and bottom-sheet variants, add the `aria-*` annotations and the analytics props. will open a PR and tag @chris @fer for review.
alexa: thanks all. tagging @a11y-bot to run full scan after PR opens :white_check_mark:
a11y-bot: accessibility-scan: queued for branch once PR opened. initial checklist passed on prototype; flagged: bottom-sheet needs `aria-modal` semantics for assistive tech.
